chapter: Instruments, first jobs and the regional scene
title: The teenage band with his brother Frank
summary: Joe and brother Frank kept a small band going at 16 or 17, with Guy Kelly occasionally and rented older players; the violinist led.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Who all was in that band, now?
Oh, we had no good musicians that you know now. Only guys...
If you can't remember their names, maybe you can remember the instrumentation.

Oh, well, sometimes... Maybe once in a while, Guy played with us. He never played with us much. When it happened, he played a cornet. Then we had a guy named... This guy Skeets I'm talkin' about, he played with some... we used to have a lot of older guys in the band sometimes, but we couldn't get... You know, me and my brother was pretty fair...
Did you want to get older guys?
No. It was because we couldn't get no young guys really to play good.

You said your preference was for the younger guys. Like, me playing now, I prefer to use older guys, because they're that much more experienced than the younger guys. Why was it that you preferred the younger guys?

Well, like I said, it wasn't too many younger guys that could play real good, not at our age. I can't remember any...there wasn't a darn kid in school... Except I had a little cousin named Lionel who played drums pretty good. But we had to rent a banjo player named (?)Sugar Do(?), and Edmond...a guy with a French name...Edmond Gautier; he played drums sometimes. I'm trying to think of the bass player's name we used to have. I can't think of his name.
My brother. Violin. Violin was always the leader, if you had one. Always. He was the one who would knock off the tunes, and then we'd play the (?).
